decision: Two separate stored statuses. The vocabulary status is a flag on the vocabulary, set ACTIVE at creation and changed only by PATCH /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}. Changing it never changes any version status, and creating a version never changes it. GET /vocabularies, the status filter and the list UI show the vocabulary status. A new version may be created for a DEPRECATED vocabulary; the vocabulary stays DEPRECATED. For the deprecated-reference check (D11) and the UI warnings (D36) a version counts as deprecated when its own status is DEPRECATED or its vocabulary status is DEPRECATED ('effectively deprecated'). This gives BP02B.05 'Full Vocabulary Deprecation' its effect without writing to every version.
basis: CDM: 'status is the vocabulary-level lifecycle status' and 'updating the vocabulary-level status or the version-level status does not create a new version'; SIMPL-18170/AC2 and SIMPL-18175/AC1 change the vocabulary status alone; BP 2B.6 'a deprecated vocabulary can still be used and referenced, but this will be discouraged'. Simplest to build and test.
owner_question: Should deprecating a vocabulary also write DEPRECATED to each of its versions, and should a new version be refused for a DEPRECATED vocabulary?

decision: Build PATCH /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions/{version} as in the OpenAPI (API only, no UI control). It sets only that version's status. Creating a version sets it ACTIVE and sets every older version that is ACTIVE to DEPRECATED, in the same transaction, with their lastUpdateDate set to the creation time. After a manual reactivation more than one version may be ACTIVE; the next new version deprecates all of them. A PATCH (vocabulary or version) that asks for the current status returns 409 with the ConflictResponse body, detail 'Vocabulary is already in status ACTIVE' or 'Vocabulary version is already in status DEPRECATED'. A status value other than ACTIVE or DEPRECATED returns 400. The UI status-change action offers only the other status. The state tables are in glossary.md.
options: Manual version change out of scope, one ACTIVE at most
Manual version change in scope, new version deprecates all older versions
basis: OpenAPI has the operation and the 409 example; CDM lists it; SIMPL-18172/AC2, 18173/AC1 and 18191/AC1 say 'all previous versions'; DDD-12.
owner_question: Confirm manual version status change is wanted, and whether two ACTIVE versions are allowed.

decision: 'Latest version' is the version with the highest version number, whatever its status. 'Latest ACTIVE version' is the highest-numbered version with version status ACTIVE and is always written out in full. GET /vocabularies, GET /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}, GET /content/{vocabularyName} and the search item with latest=true use the latest version. latestVersionHref is always filled with the href of the latest version (also on the latest version itself). 'Current version' and 'newest version' are retired; the UI column is labelled 'Latest version'.
basis: CDM 'latestVersion identifies the most recently created version'; OpenAPI summaries 'latest version metadata'; SIMPL-18184 and 18559 write 'latest ACTIVE version' explicitly.
owner_question: Retire current version and newest version in SIMPL-18161 and SIMPL-18165.

decision: No review or approval state. A new vocabulary or version that passes validation is stored and ACTIVE in the same request ('publish' = this automatic event). The manual review of BP02B.02 happens outside the system, before upload. UI labels: 'Active' shows ACTIVE, 'Deprecated' shows DEPRECATED; the API and the store use the upper-case values.

owner_question: Confirm the manual semantic review of BP02B.02 is an off-line step.

decision: Version numbers are integers. Version 1 at creation; each new version gets the highest existing number plus 1. A request to POST .../versions that carries a 'version' form field returns 400 (InputValidationProblem, in: body, name: version) and creates nothing (SIMPL-18190/AC2).

decision: Any 4xx or 5xx on POST /vocabularies or POST .../versions leaves the store unchanged: no vocabulary, no version, no status change of older versions. There is no draft or rejected state.
basis: SIMPL-18183/AC2 'not created'; SIMPL-18181/AC2 'no previous versions are deprecated'; SIMPL-18184/AC2 'no existing vocabulary versions are changed'; CDM has only ACTIVE and DEPRECATED.

decision: Two steps on every POST /vocabularies and POST .../versions: syntax, then semantic. 'Structure validation' (SIMPL-18180) is the UI word for the semantic step; there is no third step. Syntax: the file must parse as Turtle (RDF 1.1). On failure return 400 with one issue for the first parse error, location 'line N, column M', detail starting 'Encountered invalid Turtle syntax'; semantic validation does not run. Semantic (all rules run, all errors are returned in one response): S1 a literal is the object of a property declared owl:ObjectProperty in the file (detail 'Literal value for object property'); S2 an IRI or blank node is the object of a property declared owl:DatatypeProperty in the file (detail 'Resource value for datatype property'); S3 one IRI is declared both owl:ObjectProperty and owl:DatatypeProperty (detail 'Property declared as both object and datatype property'); S4 one subject has two skos:prefLabel values with the same language tag (detail 'Duplicate preferred label for the same language'); S5 one resource is typed with two classes that the file declares owl:disjointWith (detail 'Resource is an instance of disjoint classes'); S6 the file holds no triples (detail 'Vocabulary contains no statements', location 'document'); S7 a reference to an internal vocabulary or version that does not exist (D12). Location for S1 to S5 is the offending statement or resource as in the OpenAPI example. Every error blocks. Read SIMPL-18182/AC1 as: on submit, semantic validation runs after syntax validation passes.
options: Structure is part of semantic (two steps)
basis: SIMPL-18181 covers syntax only and hands over to semantic; OpenAPI examples 'Encountered invalid Turtle syntax.', 'Literal value for object property', location 'document'; CDM 'OWL semantic consistency checking'; SIMPL-18182 'unique, consistent, logically coherent'; SIMPL-18183 note 'don't fail on first issue'. The rule list is chosen to be simple to build and test.
owner_question: Give the real list of semantic and structure rules, with one example each; confirm that reporting only the first syntax error is acceptable.
later_change: untagged labels count as one language in S4 (D53); exact location text per rule (D65); at most 1000 issues (D125)

decision: Two concepts. A validation error blocks: 400 VocabularyValidationProblem, one VocabularyValidationIssue per error (type urn:problem-type:belgif:input-validation:invalidInput, in: body, name: vocabularyFile, detail, location). A validation warning never blocks: it is returned in validationWarnings of the 201 response with code, description and location, and is not stored or returned by any other endpoint. Error kinds: syntax (D9 syntax) and semantic (S1 to S7). Warning codes, closed set: externalReferenceSkipped, deprecatedVocabularyReference, semanticReasoningSkipped (reserved, not emitted in this build). syntaxError and semanticError are not warning codes. A creation that has warnings and no errors returns 201. validationWarnings is always present, as an empty array when there are none.
basis: OpenAPI keeps VocabularyValidationIssue (400) and VocabularyValidationWarning (201, 'Non-blocking'); SIMPL-18183 note 'we issue warnings for external vocabularies that cannot be resolved'; CDM 'only returned inline in the creation response'. Read SIMPL-18183/AC2 'errors or warnings' as errors only.
owner_question: Split the CDM class VocabularyValidationWarning into an error and a warning concept with these code sets.

topic: Reference to a deprecated internal version
decision: Warn, do not block. Each reference (D12) to an internal version that is effectively deprecated (D3) gives one warning: code deprecatedVocabularyReference, description "Referenced internal vocabulary '<Name>' version <n> is deprecated." followed by " Use version <m>, the latest ACTIVE version." when a latest ACTIVE version exists, location "prefix '<prefix>' -> '<namespace>'". The version is created (201). Applies to POST /vocabularies and POST .../versions.
basis: SIMPL-18184 is not consistent with itself (AC2 blocks, AC4 warns), so the next sources decide: OpenAPI 201 example with deprecatedVocabularyReference, and BP 2B.6 'A deprecated vocabulary can still be used and referenced'.
owner_question: Confirm that a deprecated reference is a warning; SIMPL-18184/AC2 then needs rewording.
later_change: no recommendation of a version of a DEPRECATED vocabulary (D47)

decision: A vocabulary reference is a namespace declared with @prefix or PREFIX in the uploaded content. It is internal when it starts with '<contentBase>/content/<Name>' (any version of <Name>, latest) or '<contentBase>/content/<Name>/versions/<n>', followed by nothing, '#' or '/'; contentBase is set in E2. An internal reference to a name or version that does not exist is a validation error S7 (400, detail "Referenced internal vocabulary '<Name>' version <n> does not exist."). A reference without version resolves to the latest version. References to the vocabulary being created or versioned are ignored. Any other namespace is external. It gives warning externalReferenceSkipped unless it (after removing a trailing '#' or '/') equals the namespace URI or an alias URI of a registered external vocabulary, or is one of rdf, rdfs, owl, xsd, skos (W3C namespaces), or is the vocabulary's own namespace (a namespace that is the prefix of at least one subject IRI in the file). The check runs on both POST /vocabularies and POST .../versions.
basis: OpenAPI warning locations use the content URL as namespace and 'prefix ... -> ...'; BP 2B.4.3 covers new vocabularies and new versions; SIMPL-18184/AC3 (missing version fails); SIMPL-18184 note 'only for INTERNAL vocabularies'.
owner_question: Confirm references are recognised by namespace prefix declarations and by the content URL, and name the namespaces that never need a cached external copy.
later_change: S7 text for a reference without a version (D47); non-numeric version is S7 (D69)

topic: File format, size and media type
decision: Turtle only. The upload limit is 5 MB (5 242 880 bytes); above it the API returns 413 with the UploadTooLargeResponse body and the UI shows its detail text. A request that is not multipart/form-data on the POST operations (or not application/json on PATCH and the search operations) returns 415. A file part that is not valid Turtle returns 400 (syntax error). A duplicate vocabulary name returns 409 (detail "Vocabulary with name '<Name>' already exists."). SIMPL-18173/AC6 'unsupported format' is the 415 case.

decision: Two Keycloak realm roles. GA_VOCABULARY_VIEWER: every GET operation and the read-only POST operations /vocabularies/searches, /external-vocabulary/searches and /external-vocabularies/content; in the UI the list, details, history and download. GA_VOCABULARY_ADMIN: everything the viewer can do plus POST /vocabularies, POST .../versions, both PATCH operations, POST and DELETE /external-vocabularies; in the UI create, new version and status change. An authenticated user with neither role gets 403 on every secured operation; a viewer gets 403 on write operations. 'The vocabulary management role' in the criteria means GA_VOCABULARY_ADMIN for writes and either role for reads; 'any role' (SIMPL-18559) means either role. The OAuth2 scopes read and write in the OpenAPI are not checked. The Governance Authority is an external actor; its users are the users holding these roles.
basis: SIMPL-18196 notes name the two roles and their meaning ('read-only operations', 'read and write operations'); SEC-05 (Tier 1 RBAC), SEC-23 (rights to roles).
owner_question: Confirm the role names and that the read-only POST searches are open to the viewer.

decision: The service validates the bearer token (JWT from Keycloak, E1) and the roles itself, so the rules can be tested without a gateway; in production the Tier 1 gateway applies the same rules first. No or invalid token: 401, problem+json, type urn:problem-type:simpl:unauthorized, title 'Unauthorized'. Valid token, missing role: 403, problem+json, type urn:problem-type:simpl:forbidden, title 'Forbidden'. Authentication and role checks run before body validation. GET /health needs no token and is outside the access rules.
basis: SIMPL-18196/AC2 and AC3, SIMPL-18162/AC3; OpenAPI security 'provided by the gateway', /health 'security: []'; SEC-12 (gateway enforces Tier 1); API-45, API-46.
owner_question: Should the OpenAPI list 401 and 403 on each operation, with these problem types?
later_change: 405 and firewall 400 come before 401 (D67); no handler without a rule (D84)

Opening the URL of the create or update form directly shows the message 'You are not authorized to perform this action.' Any 403 from the API shows the same message. A user without a token is sent to the Keycloak login page.

Field meaning: name; version = latest version number; description = latest version description (D28); status = vocabulary status (D3); createdBy and creationDate = creator and creation time of the vocabulary (version 1); lastUpdateDate = time of the last change to the vocabulary or any of its versions (new version, either status change); href = /vocabularies/<Name>; contentHref = <contentBase>/content/<Name>.

The vocabulary shows the creator of version 1.

Downloads return the stored Turtle bytes as uploaded, media type text/turtle, Content-Disposition attachment filename '<Name>.ttl' (latest) or '<Name>-v<n>.ttl'. No metadata goes into the file. 'Full details' in SIMPL-18165 and SIMPL-18166 means the version metadata (JSON, with contentHref) plus the content download; full metadata is shown on the details page.

The verb is 'register'; 'cached copy' describes what is stored. GET and DELETE /external-vocabularies/{name} return 404 when the name is unknown.

On submit the UI always sends a file: the new one, or the current content fetched from GET /content/<Name>. So a description-only change creates a new version.

decision: Name: required, 3 to 64 characters, ^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$, unique case-insensitively (409 otherwise). Description: required, 1 to 1000 characters after trimming. Changelog: required on new versions, 1 to 1000 characters after trimming. The API applies the same limits (400). The UI shows field errors under the field before submit; server errors (400 report, 409, 413) appear in a message above the form.

owner_question: Confirm case-insensitive uniqueness and the 1000-character limits.

decision: Neither search is paged. POST /vocabularies/searches takes 1 to 100 items; POST /external-vocabulary/searches takes at most 100 URIs in total (namespaceUris plus aliasUris, each array with at least 1 entry when present). More returns 400 (InputValidationProblem, in: body, name: items, namespaceUris or aliasUris). Every reference matches at most one result, so all results fit in one response: page 1, pageSize 100, total = number of items returned, totalPages 1 (0 when total is 0), and no self, first, prev, next or last links. page, pageSize or any other query parameter returns 400 (as D21). Internal search: results in request order; a missing name or version is left out (as the OpenAPI says); a repeated reference (same name and same version, or same name both without version) gives one result at its first position; {name} and {name, version} are different references and give two results even when the version is the latest. A result with latest true carries the latest version number and the vocabulary status (as D25); a result with latest false carries that version's own status. External search: URIs are normalised as in D30 (trailing '#' or '/' removed) and looked up against the namespace URI and the alias URIs; results in the order of the first matching URI, namespaceUris before aliasUris; an external vocabulary matched by several URIs appears once. A body that fits more than one oneOf branch (for example namespaceUri with aliasUri, or namespaceUri with namespaceUris) or none (empty object) returns 400, as JSON Schema oneOf requires. Roles as D16.
options: No paging, at most 100 references per request, request order, duplicates removed, two branches 400
Paging as on the GET lists with page and pageSize on the POST, ordered by name then version
basis: OpenAPI: no page parameters on either POST, 'Missing references are omitted', ExternalVocabularySearchRequest oneOf with additionalProperties false, arrays 'normalized and deduplicated'. D30 makes each URI a unique key, so a bounded request gives a bounded result; one response is simplest to build and test. D22 sets 100 as the page maximum elsewhere.
owner_question: Confirm the searches are not paged and the limit of 100 references. Add maxItems 100 (and minItems 1 on the external arrays) to the request schemas, and state the result order in the operation descriptions.
later_change: issue names fixed (D68); issue named after the array (D137)

topic: Decided behaviour the OpenAPI file does not yet show
decision: The decisions win over the OpenAPI file (source hierarchy). Writers build and test the decided behaviour, not the file, on these points: 401 and 403 on every secured operation (D17); name filter relaxed (D19); pageSize maximum 100 (D22); createdBy on version objects (D27); validationWarnings always present with the closed code set (D10); description and changelog 1 to 1000 characters (D37); version form field rejected (D7); latestVersionHref always filled (D5); unknown query parameters rejected (D21); search limits (D38). The writers do not edit the file in specs/api. A writer who generates stubs, clients or contract tests from it adds these points by hand in its own build. No decision is changed by this entry.
options: Build from the decisions and add the deltas by hand
Build from the OpenAPI file as it stands
basis: decisions.md source hierarchy (decisions above OpenAPI); D5, D7, D10, D17, D19, D21, D22, D27, D37 already settle each point; P-002 lists the gaps.
owner_question: Update the OpenAPI file: add 401 and 403 responses with the D17 problem types; VocabularyNameQuery pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9]+$ with minLength 1; PageSizeQuery maximum 100; createdBy on VocabularyMetadata and VocabularyVersionMetadataResponse; validationWarnings required and VocabularyValidationWarning.code as an enum; minLength 1 and maxLength 1000 on description and changelog; additionalProperties false on CreateNewVocabularyVersionPayload; latestVersionHref not nullable; a note that unknown query parameters return 400.

decision: Treat the security scheme as OpenID Connect through the Keycloak realm of E1. Clients (the UI and the tests) get a bearer token from Keycloak and request no scopes beyond openid; the scopes read and write are neither requested nor checked (D16). The backend validates the token and the realm roles (D17). Writers ignore the placeholder URLs of OAuth2Auth; a generated client or API console is configured with the Keycloak URLs of E1 and E2.
options: OpenID Connect through Keycloak with roles, scopes ignored
Enforce the read and write scopes of the file
basis: D16 (roles, scopes not checked), D17 (service validates token and roles), E1 (Keycloak realm simpl), SEC-07 (Tier 1 authentication through OpenID Connect and Keycloak).
owner_question: Replace OAuth2Auth with an openIdConnect scheme pointing at the Tier 1 Keycloak discovery URL, drop the read and write scopes, and describe the two realm roles per operation.

topic: Test basis for operations without a story
decision: The OpenAPI responses plus D4, D16, D17, D22, D27, D29 and D30 are the test basis for the external vocabulary operations and the manual version status change; the missing stories are a backlog item, not a blocker. External vocabularies: POST /external-vocabularies returns 201 with Location and href /external-vocabularies/<Name> and the ExternalVocabulary body with createdBy and creationDate; invalid Turtle returns 400 with one issue as the D9 syntax error (in: body, name: vocabularyFile), no semantic errors and no warnings; 409, 413 and 415 as D15 and D30. GET /external-vocabularies is paged as D22, default and only order name ascending, no filter or sort parameters (others 400 as D21). GET /external-vocabularies/{name} returns 200 with ExternalVocabulary. GET /external-vocabularies/{name}/content returns the stored Turtle bytes, text/turtle, filename '<Name>.ttl'. DELETE /external-vocabularies/{name} returns 204 and removes metadata and content; a later GET returns 404; internal vocabularies already stored are not touched. Every 404 on an external vocabulary path uses the ExternalVocabularyNotFoundResponse body with detail "External vocabulary with name '<Name>' was not found." and one issue (in: path, name: name). Version status change: as D4, and 404 (VocabularyNotFoundResponse) for an unknown name or version.
options: Accept the decisions and the OpenAPI as the test basis and log the missing stories
basis: P-004 option 2; D30 and D4 already fix the behaviour; the OpenAPI states 201, 204, 404 and the content media type; ExternalVocabularyNotFoundResponse exists for external lookups (P-005); name ascending matches GET /vocabularies (D23) and is simplest (P-006).
owner_question: Add one API story for external vocabulary registration (register, list, read, content, delete) and one for the version status change, with criteria taken from D30, D41 and D4. Point the 404 of GET and DELETE /external-vocabularies/{name} at ExternalVocabularyNotFoundResponse, and give POST /external-vocabularies a 400 example with a syntax error only.
later_change: 404 text for the content lookup by namespace (D66)

decision: Registering and removing an external vocabulary is an administration action outside the BP02B steps in this build. A user with GA_VOCABULARY_ADMIN (D16) does it at any time through the operations of D41. The system enforces no order: an internal vocabulary or version created before the external vocabulary is registered is stored, with warning externalReferenceSkipped for that namespace (D12); after registering, the Governance Authority may create a new version to clear the warning. Removal is allowed while internal versions reference the namespace: DELETE /external-vocabularies/{name} returns 204 with no reference check and no warning (as D41). Stored internal versions keep their content and status. A later creation or new version that references the removed namespace gets externalReferenceSkipped.
options: Add register and remove steps to BP02B, removal allowed without check
Add the steps, removal refused while an ACTIVE internal version references the namespace
basis: BP02B Overview names registration but no step; D12 already turns an unregistered namespace into a warning, so the order changes a warning, never the stored result; D41 fixes DELETE as 204 with stored internal vocabularies untouched. A reference check on removal would need parsing every stored version; no criterion asks for it. Simplest to build and test.
owner_question: Process owner: add steps 'Register external vocabulary' and 'Remove external vocabulary' to BP02B (before BP02B.01 and BP02B.04), or keep them outside the process? Confirm that removing a referenced external vocabulary is allowed without a check.

decision: Changes to the same vocabulary are serialised: POST .../versions, PATCH /vocabularies/{vocabularyName} and PATCH .../versions/{version} for one vocabulary run one after another, and each sees the stored result of the one before. So two overlapping version creations both succeed with 201 and get numbers n+1 and n+2; the later one deprecates the earlier one (D4); the store never holds two versions with the same number. A version creation and a status PATCH that overlap give the result of running them in one order or the other; both orders are valid outcomes (D4 allows two ACTIVE versions after a reactivation). Two identical PATCH requests that overlap give 200 and then 409 (same status, D4). Two POST /vocabularies with the same name (compared case-insensitively, D37) that overlap give one 201 and one 409; only one vocabulary is stored. Changes to different vocabularies are not serialised against each other. Each request runs its whole change in one store transaction, so a failure leaves nothing half done (D8). This build runs one backend instance: a lock per vocabulary name (lower case) in the service plus one store transaction per request meets the rule. Time spent waiting for the lock counts towards the request timeout of D44; when it runs out the request returns 503 as D44 and stores nothing. No new status code: overlapping creations never return 409. Test: with version 1 stored, send 5 POST .../versions in parallel; expect five 201 responses, versions 2 to 6 each exactly once, distinct Location headers, version 6 ACTIVE and versions 1 to 5 DEPRECATED.
options: Serialise per vocabulary: numbers n+1 and n+2, the later version deprecates the earlier
Optimistic check: the second request returns 409 and stores nothing
Leave it to the store and accept the risk
basis: OWT-A10 (no half-done change, defined outcomes); D7 (highest plus 1), D4 (same transaction), D8. The OpenAPI lists no 409 on POST .../versions, so serialising needs no API change, and its outcome is deterministic enough to test. An optimistic 409 would make a parallel test depend on timing.
owner_question: Confirm that overlapping changes to one vocabulary are serialised rather than refused, and say whether production runs several backend instances (then the serialisation must hold across them, for example in the store).
later_change: lock wait at most 30 s (D71); one replica only (D81); conditional store update instead of the in-process lock (D82); test with at most 4 parallel writes (D119)

topic: Store and identity provider slow or down
decision: Store (Fuseki, E3): connect timeout 2 s, response timeout 10 s per store call. Read-only store queries are retried at most 2 times on a connection failure or timeout, after 200 ms and then 400 ms. Store updates are never retried by the service. When the store stays unreachable or times out, the operation returns 503, application/problem+json, type urn:problem-type:belgif:serviceUnavailable, title 'Service Unavailable', detail 'The vocabulary store is not available. Retry later.', with header Retry-After: 5. A store error that is not a timeout or a connection failure stays 500 (InternalServerErrorResponse). Each write is one store transaction, so after a 503 the store holds the whole change or none of it; when the store was unreachable it holds none (D8). After a 503 on a write the client checks with GET before it resubmits. Identity provider (Keycloak, E1): the service validates tokens locally with the realm keys. It fetches the keys at start and again when a token names an unknown key id, timeout 2 s, no retry inside a request. Cached keys keep working while Keycloak is down. When a token names a key id that is not cached and the keys cannot be fetched, the request fails closed with 503 (same body, detail 'The identity provider is not available. Retry later.'); it is never accepted without a signature check. This runs before the role and body checks (D17). GET /health: 503 DOWN when the store does not answer within 2 s; 200 DEGRADED when the store answers but no realm keys are loaded and Keycloak does not answer; otherwise 200 UP. UI: a 503 is shown like a 500 (the generic error with the advice to retry or contact support, SIMPL-18172/AC3, D24). Tests: start the backend with the store URL on a port where nothing listens; GET /vocabularies and POST /vocabularies return 503 with this body and Retry-After, and GET /health returns 503 DOWN. The identity provider case is covered by unit tests in the code, not by the API tests.
options: Timeout and no retry on writes, 503 with a problem type, fail closed with 503
Retry reads with backoff, no retry on writes, 500 for all dependency failures
Leave to the build, test only the 500 outcome
basis: MSV-06 (timeout, retries with backoff, what the caller sees per dependency); OWT-A10 (fail closed); SIMPL-18172/AC3 (advised to retry); OpenAPI /health already uses 503 with DOWN and DEGRADED. 503 tells the client to retry, 500 stays for defects. Problem+json as every other error of this component. This refines D8: a write that times out after the store received it may have committed, all or nothing.
owner_question: API owner: add a 503 ServiceUnavailableResponse (belgif serviceUnavailable, Retry-After) to every secured operation. Confirm the timeouts and that a missing identity provider fails with 503, not 401.
later_change: store update timeout 45 s (D71); key refetch at most once per 10 s; unknown key id inside the window is 401 (D88); circuit breakers, open gives 503 at once (D103); lazy first key fetch allowed (D108); health does not fetch keys (D134)

topic: How consumers learn of publication and deprecation
decision: Pull only. Vocabulary Manager publishes no events in this build. Consumers (Schema Manager, D1) read the state at use time through the search operations (D38) and the content operations (D29). The content of a stored version never changes, so a consumer may keep a copy of it, but it reads the status again through a search each time it validates a schema. Telling the providers whose schemas use a version that has just been deprecated is an off-line task of the Governance Authority, like the email route of BP02B Assumptions; the system sends nothing. The deprecation warnings that consumers see come from the status in the search results and the warnings of D11 and D36.
options: Pull only: consumers read at use time, no event, no notice to providers
Publish events on publication and on each status change
Pull for Schema Manager, plus a notice to providers outside the system
basis: No input names an event bus or an event for this component (api-review, API-62 not applicable); Schema Manager is outside this build (D1) and is a caller of the search and content operations. Deviates from MSV-03 (SHOULD): no event, because no consumer of an event is specified and pull at use time sees every change. Simplest to build and test.
owner_question: Does Schema Manager keep copies of vocabulary status, so that it needs an event on publication and on each status change? Who tells the providers that a version they use was deprecated?

topic: Limits and abuse cases on version creation
decision: Identical-version check: POST .../versions is refused with 409 (ConflictResponse body, type urn:problem-type:simpl:conflict, detail "Version <n> of vocabulary '<Name>' already has this content and description.") when the uploaded file bytes equal the stored content bytes of the latest version (D5) and the trimmed description equals its description. The changelog is not compared. Nothing is stored (D8). The check runs after the authentication, role, 404 and field checks (400, 413, 415) and before validation. A description-only change still creates a new version (D33). UI: no confirmation step (SIMPL-18172/AC2 submits and creates); the new version form shows the fixed line 'Submitting creates version <n+1> and deprecates every older ACTIVE version.', where n is the latest version number; a 409 appears in the message above the form (D37). No call-rate limit in the service in this build; in production the Tier 1 gateway applies the platform call-rate limit (OWA-API4), outside this build. Abuse cases, as decisions: (1) resubmitting the latest version unchanged returns 409 and deprecates nothing; (2) a viewer or a user without a role who tries to create a version gets 403 (D16, D17); (3) an admin who churns changed versions is not stopped by the service; recovery is a PATCH back to ACTIVE (D4) and the actions are traceable through createdBy (D27).
options: Refuse identical versions and add a UI confirmation; no rate limit
Add a rate limit per user and vocabulary at the gateway, plus the identical-version check
Accept the risk: admin role only, recovery by PATCH
basis: OWA-API6 (a check on a flow that costs other parties), OWT-A06 (abuse cases written down); acceptance criteria rank above the business process, and SIMPL-18172/AC2 has no confirmation, so the UI informs instead of asking. Byte comparison is simplest to build and test; D33 resends the stored bytes, so an unchanged form gives the same bytes. 409 is the component's status for a request that conflicts with the stored state (D4, D30, D37).
owner_question: API owner: add 409 to POST /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions. Confirm byte equality as the identical test, and set the gateway call-rate limit for write operations.
later_change: full order of checks on writes (D51)

decision: Deprecated reference (D11): the description is "Referenced internal vocabulary '<Name>' version <n> is deprecated.". The sentence " Use version <m>, the latest ACTIVE version." is added only when the vocabulary status is ACTIVE and a version <m> other than <n> has version status ACTIVE. When the vocabulary status is DEPRECATED the description is followed by " The vocabulary '<Name>' is deprecated." and no version is recommended. Missing reference (D12, S7): with a version "Referenced internal vocabulary '<Name>' version <n> does not exist."; without a version (name unknown) "Referenced internal vocabulary '<Name>' does not exist.".
options: Recommend only a different, really ACTIVE version
Always recommend the highest ACTIVE version
basis: D3 makes every version of a DEPRECATED vocabulary effectively deprecated, so recommending one of them contradicts the warning. The S7 text without a version is what run 4's build returned.

decision: Keep the types the OpenAPI and D44 fix: urn:problem-type:belgif:... for 400, 404, 500 and 503. Use urn:problem-type:simpl:... for 401, 403, 409, 413 and 415 (D17, D4, D15). This is a recorded deviation from API-46 for the four belgif codes; the code writer lists it in DEVIATIONS.md and the suite checks API-46 only on the simpl codes.
options: OpenAPI belgif types stay (deviation from API-46)
basis: Source hierarchy: the OpenAPI is the exact source for the wire format; API-46 is a SHOULD. Changing the published types is the API owner's call.
owner_question: API owner: move the four belgif types to simpl URNs (API-46), or record the exception.

decision: A GET, PATCH or DELETE whose path name or version breaks its pattern (D37 for names, a positive integer for versions) returns 400 InputValidationProblem with one issue (type urn:problem-type:belgif:input-validation:schemaViolation, in: path, name: the parameter). A valid name that is not stored returns 404 (D24, D41). Tests prove 'nothing stored' through the list with a name filter, not through a GET on the rejected name.

owner_question: Confirm 400 for a path value that breaks the pattern.

topic: Click on the active sort column
decision: UI list: a click on a sortable column that is not the active sort sorts it ascending. A click on the active sort column reverses its order. So on the default list (Name ascending) the first click on Name sorts descending.
basis: Common table behaviour; run 4's build did this, and with 'always ascending' the first click on the default column would change nothing visible. Run 4 section 3.2.

topic: Order of checks on write operations
decision: Every write runs its checks in this order and stops at the first failure: 401, 403 (D17); 415 media type; 413 size; 400 request shape (path values D49, unknown fields and parameters D52, field rules D37, the version field D7); 404 vocabulary or version not found; 409 conflicts (duplicate name D15 and D37, same status D4, identical version D46); then validation of the content (syntax, then semantic, D9). So a duplicate name with invalid content gives 409, and a malformed request to an unknown name gives 400.
basis: Checks that need no store run first: cheaper and they reveal nothing about stored names (OWT-A01). Run 4's build used this order.
later_change: 406 sits between 403 and 415 (D63)

decision: Any form field or JSON property the OpenAPI schema does not define returns 400 InputValidationProblem with one issue per unknown name (in: body), also where the schema does not say additionalProperties: false. Any query parameter on a POST, PATCH or DELETE returns 400 (in: query), as D21 does for GET. A query parameter given twice returns 400.
basis: OWA-API3 (no mass assignment) and D21; run 4's build did this.
later_change: part with an empty name is unknown (D70); one issue per repeated parameter (D138)

decision: For S4, a literal without a language tag counts as one language ('no language'). Two untagged skos:prefLabel values on one subject are an S4 error. One untagged and one tagged value are not.
basis: SKOS integrity condition S14 (at most one prefLabel per language tag), reading 'no tag' as one value.

decision: Paths match the stored name exactly. /vocabularies/HEALTH for a stored 'Health' returns 404. The case-insensitive rule of D37 applies only to uniqueness on create and registration. Search by name (D38) is exact too; the list name filter stays case-insensitive (D19).
basis: A path names one resource; exact match is simplest and gives one canonical URL. Run 4's build did this.

topic: Problem texts the decisions do not give
decision: Fixed: version not found "Version <n> of vocabulary '<Name>' was not found."; external namespace conflict "An external vocabulary with namespace or alias '<uri>' is already registered.". 405 and an unknown path return application/problem+json with status 405 and 404; their type and detail are free. Field messages (400 issues) are free text. Tests check status, type, issue 'in' and 'name', and only the detail texts a decision fixes.
options: Fix only what users act on
basis: Texts a user or client acts on are fixed; the rest would only make tests brittle.
later_change: '<uri>' is the URI as sent (D66)

decision: Name: the D37 rules, unique case-insensitively among external vocabularies (409). Internal and external names are separate: an external vocabulary may share a name with an internal one. aliasUris: one multipart part 'aliasUris' per URI, optional, at most 20; an alias that equals the namespace URI or repeats another alias (compared as D30) returns 400 (in: body, name: aliasUris). description: optional, at most 1000 characters after trimming.
options: One name space for internal and external
basis: Paths are separate (/vocabularies, /external-vocabularies), so separate names are simplest; D30 and D37 for the rest.
owner_question: Confirm separate names and the alias limit of 20.
later_change: one URI per part (D70); alias order as sent (D73)

decision: Relative IRIs in uploaded Turtle resolve against the content URL of the new version: <contentBase>/content/<Name>/versions/<n> (D26). The stored bytes stay as uploaded (D29); the base is used only for validation.
basis: Run 4's build did this; it keeps uploads with relative IRIs valid.
later_change: also for external files (D124)

decision: Times are stored and returned in UTC to the second, ISO 8601 with 'Z' (2026-11-18T09:27:00Z). Sort, ties and filters (D20, D23) use this value. The name sort compares by code point, so 'AZ' comes before 'Ab'.
basis: Clients see what is sorted and filtered. Names always start with a capital (D37), so code point order differs only inside names. Run 4's build did both.

Status change: action label 'Deprecate' on an ACTIVE vocabulary and 'Activate' on a DEPRECATED one, no confirmation dialog, success message 'Status of <Name> changed to <Active|Deprecated>.'. topic: Run environment from the build profile
decision: The build profile of the run (build.yaml) fixes ports, URLs, issuer and the test users' access; E2's ports and URLs are defaults only and every value is read from environment variables, so code and suite run unchanged on any ports. The store is never reset by the tests: every scenario creates its own data with a unique run id and does not depend on an empty store (counts and lists are checked through filters on its own names). E3's reset sentence is withdrawn; the rest of E3 stands.
options: E2 and E3 win, profile follows
basis: Run 4: both writers found the clash independently. Unique data per scenario lets several runs share one stack and needs no test-only endpoint.

decision: Submit is disabled only while the upload check of D13 shows a syntax error or a refused file (D76). Field errors of D37 do not disable it. A click on Submit with field errors sends nothing, keeps the errors under the fields and moves the focus to the first field with an error.
basis: D13 names the upload check only; tests then need no build-specific state of the button.
later_change: all fields checked on Submit, no layout shift (D101)

decision: The Accept header is checked after 401 and 403 and before 415 (D51). A JSON operation accepts application/json, application/problem+json, */* or no Accept header; a content download accepts text/turtle, */* or no Accept header. Anything else returns 406, application/problem+json, type urn:problem-type:simpl:notAcceptable, title 'Not Acceptable', no issues.
basis: The OpenAPI lists 406 on every operation; problem types as D48.
later_change: application/* accepted (D127)

topic: Latest ACTIVE version link in the UI
decision: The UI follows D47: for a version of a DEPRECATED vocabulary it shows 'This version is deprecated.' and no 'Latest ACTIVE version' line. A version never links to itself: when the latest ACTIVE version is the version shown, the line is left out.
basis: D3 makes every version of a DEPRECATED vocabulary effectively deprecated; recommending one of them contradicts D47.

topic: Location texts of issues and warnings
decision: Locations follow the OpenAPI examples. Syntax: 'line <n>, column <m>' (D9, column only when the parser gives one, D60). S1 and S2: statement '<subject> <predicate> <object>' with full IRIs and the literal as written. S3: resource '<property IRI>'. S4: resource '<subject IRI>', language '<tag>' ('none' for an untagged label, D53), one issue per subject and language. S5: resource '<IRI>'. S6: 'document'. S7, externalReferenceSkipped and deprecatedVocabularyReference: prefix '<prefix>' -> '<namespace>'.
basis: OpenAPI examples at the validation and warning responses; one issue per language makes S4 issues distinct.
later_change: literal in N-Triples form (D140)

decision: Internal vocabulary not found: "Vocabulary with name '<Name>' was not found." with one issue (in: path, name: vocabularyName). POST /external-vocabularies/content with an unknown URI: 404, ExternalVocabularyNotFoundResponse, detail "External vocabulary with namespaceUri '<uri>' was not found." with one issue (in: body, name: namespaceUri); D41's name text stays for the paths with a name. In D55's conflict text and in these texts '<uri>' is the URI as the client sent it in this request.
basis: OpenAPI examples of the 404 responses.

decision: Order before any operation runs: a method the server does not know (for example QUERY) returns 405; a path the firewall refuses (encoded slash, control character) returns 400 problem+json, type urn:problem-type:belgif:badRequest, no issues; then the token (D17), so an unknown path gives 401 without a token and 404 with one. /actuator paths do not exist on the API port: 401 without a token, 404 with one. Health and metrics are served on a separate management port that is not exposed outside the deployment; GET /health on the API stays as D44.
basis: Matches what a standard HTTP stack does before authentication; keeps management endpoints off the public port (MACH-08, OWA rules).
later_change: metrics content and trace forwarding fixed (D86); management port on an internal network only (D98); HEAD and OPTIONS also 405 (D126)

decision: Internal search: an invalid item gives in: body, name: items[<i>].name or items[<i>].version (index from 0). A body that matches no or several oneOf branches gives in: body, name: body. Over 100 URIs in an external search gives name: aliasUris when both arrays are present, otherwise the name of the array sent.
basis: Confirms the build of run 5; names point at the offending element (API rules on issue names).

decision: A namespace '<contentBase>/content/<Name>/versions/<v>' where <v> is not a positive integer is an S7 error with the text of D47 using <v> as given. A namespace '<contentBase>/content/' with no name, or with a name that breaks D37's pattern, is external (externalReferenceSkipped as D12).
basis: A malformed version is a mistake the author should see; silent reading as latest hides it.

decision: Downloads: Content-Type exactly 'text/turtle', no charset, bytes as uploaded (D29). A 0-byte vocabularyFile passes the field check and fails validation with S6 (400, location 'document'). Each aliasUris part holds one URI; commas are not split, so 'a,b' is one URI and fails D73. External registration rejects a file with no statements: 400 with one issue, detail 'Vocabulary contains no statements', in: body, name: vocabularyFile. A multipart part with an empty name is an unknown field: 400, in: body, name: ''.
basis: Confirms the build where it was sound; an empty external vocabulary can never be a lookup target.
later_change: empty part name no longer 400 (D121)

decision: A create or new version with a file at the 5 MB limit completes within 30 s (Q1); the storage design must meet this. D44's 10 s store response timeout applies to reads; a store update may take up to 45 s before 503. The wait for the per-vocabulary lock (D43) is at most 30 s, then 503 as D44. Writes to different vocabularies may wait for each other in the store; that wait counts towards the same budgets.
options: Keep 10 s for all store calls
basis: Run 6: a 5 MB upload needed about 20 s in Fuseki and failed at 10 s; a correct upload at the decided limit must succeed.

decision: Filters: 'Name contains', 'Vocabulary status', 'Created on'. Row actions: 'View vocabulary details', 'History', 'Download vocabulary', 'Update', 'Deprecate' or 'Activate' (D60). After a successful creation the UI opens the details page of the new vocabulary and shows the D14 notification and warnings there. Failed status change: 404 shows 'Vocabulary not found. The status was not changed.'; 500 and 503 show 'The vocabulary status could not be updated.' followed by the D60 text and the problem detail. Loading the list or history: 500 and 503 show the D34 or D35 text and the problem detail, not the D60 text. List deprecation: the warning icon's accessible name and tooltip is D36's text; it is not visible row text.
basis: Confirms the build of run 5 where no Figma label is known; Figma labels replace them when the owners supply them.
later_change: also after a new version (D113); one alert element per event (D114)

decision: namespaceUri, aliasUris and sourceUri must be absolute URIs (RFC 3986, with a scheme); otherwise 400, in: body, name: the field (also in the body of POST /external-vocabularies/content). They are stored and returned exactly as sent; aliases come back in the order sent. Only comparisons (uniqueness, lookups, D12) remove a trailing '#' or '/' (D30).
basis: Returning what was sent keeps the cached copy faithful; D30 already compares normalised.

decision: Create form: /vocabularies/new. New version form: /vocabularies/<Name>/versions/new. 'new' cannot be a vocabulary name because names start with an upper-case letter (D37).
basis: D18 needs fixed URLs to test direct access.

topic: UI semantics the tests may use
decision: UI tests use only roles, decided labels and decided texts, never test ids or names taken from a build. The UI provides: the list and the version history as tables with column headers named as in D23 and D35; one actions menu button per row named 'Actions for <Name>' (version rows 'Actions for version <n>'); the version panel as a region named 'Version <n>'; the validation report as a region named 'Validation report' and warnings as 'Validation warnings'; success messages with role status; error messages with role alert; form fields labelled as D60.
basis: Accessible names serve users and tests alike (NFR-10); the run 5 suite review found UI tests that took names from the build.
later_change: report is a region with an alert line inside (D90)

decision: The 5 MB limit of D15 is on the vocabularyFile part. The whole multipart request may be at most 6 MB; above that the API returns 413 with the same body. In the UI a chosen file over 5 MB gives a field error under 'Vocabulary file': 'The file is larger than 5 MB.', and Submit is disabled (D62). The 413 detail above the form appears only when the server answers 413.
basis: Users think of the file size; the request cap bounds the text fields (NFR-04).

topic: Paths that can match the same URL
decision: In this contract a fixed segment wins over a path parameter: /vocabularies/searches and /external-vocabularies/content are never read as a name. No stored name can equal them, because names start with an upper-case letter (D37). A method those fixed paths do not offer (for example GET /vocabularies/searches) returns 405. A later contract version should move the operations so no two paths overlap (SOA-09).
basis: Writers do not edit the contract (D39); D37 makes the overlap harmless here.

decision: self, first, prev, next and last keep every query parameter of the request (filters and sort) with its value; only page changes.
basis: A link that drops the filter would page through another list.
later_change: page and pageSize always present (D111)

decision: The decisions differ from the published OpenAPI here; writers build and test the decisions, fuzzing treats these as expected (fuzz-known.yaml), and the owners should put them in the next contract version. Stricter: 401 and 403 on every secured operation (D17); pageSize at most 100 (D22); name 3 to 64 characters and pattern on create (D37); description and changelog 1 to 1000 characters after trimming (D37, D56); unknown fields, unknown or repeated query parameters and parts with an empty name rejected (D21, D52, D70); version form field rejected (D7); search array sizes and totals (D38); at most 20 aliasUris, no duplicates (D56); absolute URIs (D73); file must be valid, non-empty Turtle, not any binary (D9, D70); invalid path values 400 (D49); 406 (D63); 405 on undeclared methods (D67); multipart request at most 6 MB (D76). Wider: name filter pattern relaxed (D19); createdBy on version objects (D27); validationWarnings always present (D10); latestVersionHref always filled (D5).
basis: Step 30 item 8; replaces the shorter list of D39.
later_change: build delivers openapi-decided.yaml (D87); format int32 and maximum on every integer (D91); D110 details added; D116 formats added; empty part name dropped from the list (D121); truncated field (D125)

decision: Logs never contain the email or name of a user. They carry the token subject (sub) as the user id. createdBy in the data stays as D27.
basis: GDPR data minimisation; logs are kept and copied more widely than the store.

decision: Accepted risk for this build: exactly one backend instance runs (the deployment sets one replica). D43's in-process lock is valid only then. Running more instances needs a store-side check first (for example a conditional update on the latest version number); that is a later decision.
basis: The design load (Q4) fits one instance.
later_change: withdrawn by D82 (D82)

decision: Measured on the build's own stack at the design load of Q4, after warm-up. Reads (lists, details, searches, downloads under 1 MB): p95 at most 300 ms. Create or new version: p95 at most 3 s for files up to 1 MB; at most 30 s for a file at the 5 MB limit (D71). Throughput: 20 reads per second and 1 write per second sustained with no errors.
basis: Step 30 item 6 (NFR-01, NFR-02); no project NFR gives a number, so the target is provisional and fits the design load of Q4.
later_change: throughput as offered rate, 5 MB writes measured apart (D99); per operation (D136)

decision: The limits of D15, D22, D37, D38, D56, D71 and D76 are the component's limits (NFR-04). Each is enforced with a defined error, and each has a test at the limit and one above.
basis: Step 30 item 6 (NFR-01, NFR-02); no project NFR gives a number, so the target is provisional and fits the design load of Q4.
later_change: at most 4 uploads in parallel per instance (D92)

decision: Availability 99.5 % per month in office hours (08:00 to 18:00 CET, working days). Recovery time 30 minutes, recovery point 24 hours. Daily backup of the whole store, kept outside the host. Restore never leaves the store emptier than before: it loads the backup into a new dataset, checks the count, and only then replaces the old one. A backup and restore round trip is tested on every build.
basis: Step 30 item 6 (NFR-01, NFR-02); no project NFR gives a number, so the target is provisional and fits the design load of Q4.
later_change: writes after the backup are lost within the RPO; backend stopped during a restore; schedule and copy target delivered as examples (D89)

decision: Design load: 20 concurrent users of the Governance Authority, 1000 vocabularies, 20 versions each, files up to 5 MB, 10 consuming services that search. One backend instance (D81); scale up, not out, until a store-side check exists.
basis: Step 30 item 6 (NFR-01, NFR-02); no project NFR gives a number, so the target is provisional and fits the design load of Q4.
later_change: scale out allowed (D82); seed 1000 by 20 versions (D99); two instances on the finish line, D81 sentence replaced (D102)

decision: Backend line coverage at least 80 % and branch coverage at least 60 % from the build's own tests; no HIGH or CRITICAL finding in own images and dependencies (Trivy); the reference check needs at most one store query per upload (bounded, NFR-05).
basis: Step 30 item 6 (NFR-01, NFR-02); no project NFR gives a number, so the target is provisional and fits the design load of Q4.
later_change: no store query without LIMIT (D85); format, lint and UI tests on the finish line (D95)

decision: WCAG 2.1 AA: no axe violations on the list, details and both form pages; every action reachable by keyboard.
basis: Step 30 item 6 (NFR-01, NFR-02); no project NFR gives a number, so the target is provisional and fits the design load of Q4.

decision: Tokens must carry the audience 'vocabulary-manager-be'; Keycloak adds it with an audience mapper on the clients that call the API (vocabulary-manager-ui and the test client). Tokens without it get 401. The accepted issuer is one configured URL (ISSUER_URI, default http://localhost:<KEYCLOAK_PORT>/realms/simpl); other issuers get 401.
basis: Environment choice (step 30 items 5 and 7).
later_change: tested through E7 (E7)

decision: From guidelines/reuse-catalogue.yaml: identity provider Keycloak (E1); RDF store Apache Jena Fuseki (E3); in production the Tier 1 gateway (Spring Cloud Gateway) does authorisation first, the build checks tokens itself (D17); secrets from environment variables locally, OpenBao in production; UI on the stack of participant-fe-components (Vue 3, PrimeVue unstyled, TailwindCSS), built here because the library is not available to the factory. Not needed: relational store, messaging (pull only, D45), object storage, connector, http-client (no outgoing calls except the realm keys).
basis: Environment choice (step 30 items 5 and 7).
later_change: REUSE.md row per own infrastructure component (D93); named libraries for SPARQL, keys and tracing (D94)

decision: The realm 'simpl' has a second public client 'vocabulary-tests-noaud' without the audience mapper, and a second realm 'simpl-other' with client 'vocabulary-tests' (with the mapper) and the same three test users of E1. Both allow the password grant. A token from 'vocabulary-tests-noaud' gets 401 (wrong audience); a token from realm 'simpl-other' gets 401 (wrong issuer). The build profile gives their token URLs to the suite.
basis: E5 is security behaviour at the boundary, so the independent suite must be able to prove it.

decision: D43's outcomes stay, but the service holds no lock state. Each write to a vocabulary is a conditional store update: it succeeds only when the latest version number (or, for a status change, the status) is still the one the request read. When the condition fails the service reads again and retries, at most 5 times within the budget of D71; then 503 as D44. A create checks the case-insensitive name in the same update. So several backend instances may run on one store. D81 is withdrawn. The build proves it with its own test of two service instances on one store; the suite's D43 test stays.
basis: ARCH-07 (MUST) asks for stateless instances; the store already runs one write at a time, so the condition costs little.
later_change: validation outside the retry loop (D92)

decision: The store accepts no anonymous access. It has two users: a read user and an update user, with passwords from the environment (OpenBao in production, E6). The backend uses the read user for queries and the update user for writes. Admin endpoints are off, or need a third admin user that only the backup and restore scripts use. The store sits on an internal network of the deployment and publishes no port to the host; backup and restore reach it from inside that network.
basis: Zero trust and defence in depth (reuse catalogue patterns, OWT-A02, OWT-A07); REUSE.md of run 7 claimed both and the store link had neither.
later_change: Keycloak port on 127.0.0.1 only (D98); also no debug port (D107)

decision: Every operation of the OpenAPI has an explicit role rule (D16). A request that matches no declared operation never reaches a handler: 401 without a token, 404 with one (D67), and it is never served by a handler that has no rule. The build fails at start, or in its own test, when a handler exists without a role rule. Nothing is allowed unless a rule allows it.
basis: OWASP A01 (deny by default); the run 7 role gate let unlisted routes through.
later_change: 405 before 401 and 404 (D139)

decision: Filtering, sorting and paging run in the store: every list query has ORDER BY, LIMIT and OFFSET, and the total comes from a COUNT query. No store query runs without a LIMIT; the highest LIMIT is 100 rows plus one, except where a decision fixes a bound (search: at most 100 references, D38; reference check: one query per upload, Q5). The version list of the details page uses the same paging (D35).
basis: NFR-05 and the design load of Q4 (1000 vocabularies, 20 000 versions).

decision: Metrics in Prometheus format on the management port (D67) at /actuator/prometheus: per operation the request count, the error count by status and the duration. The service reads the W3C traceparent header and X-Correlation-Id (creating them when absent), returns X-Correlation-Id, writes both in every log line, and forwards both on its calls to the store and to the identity provider. No tracing backend is part of the build.
basis: NFR-08, MSV-09 (MUST) and MSV-10; D67 already put metrics on the management port.
later_change: JSON log lines with operationId, vocabularyName and version (D96)

decision: The build delivers in docs/: a logical data model (entities, attributes, identifiers and relations, as tables and one diagram) traced to the CDM of D2; a physical model for the RDF store as SHACL shapes of each named graph, which the build's own tests run against stored data; and openapi-decided.yaml, the published OpenAPI with every change of D79 applied. The files in specs/api stay unchanged (D39). Step 70 keeps fuzzing the published contract.
basis: DATA-02, DATA-03 and DATA-22 to DATA-25 ask for models of persisted data; MACH-03 and DATA-27 for a contract that matches the behaviour.
later_change: request validation tied to openapi-decided.yaml (D93); LDM uses the CDM in input/cdm (D97)

decision: The service fetches the realm keys again at most once per 10 s. A token whose key id is not cached gets one fetch when the last fetch is older than 10 s. Inside the 10 s window, or when the fetched keys still lack the key id, the token gets 401 (invalid token, D17). 503 stays for the case where the keys cannot be fetched at all (D44).
basis: Cooldown protects the identity provider from tokens with made-up key ids (OWT-A10); the build of run 8 already did this.
later_change: 503 after a failed fetch (D129)

decision: A restore brings the store back to the backup; writes made after that backup are lost, which is within the recovery point of Q3 (24 h). Before a restore the backend is stopped (or scaled to 0), so no write lands during it; it is started again after the count check. The build delivers the backup script, an example schedule (cron line or Kubernetes CronJob) and a configurable copy target outside the host; installing the schedule is an operations task, documented in docs/.
basis: Simplest procedure that meets Q3; merging later changes is not worth its cost at this load.

decision: The validation report is a region (section with aria-label) named 'Validation report' that holds the list of issues. The region has no role of its own beyond region. Inside it, a first line with role alert says how many errors were found ('<n> errors found'), so screen readers announce it. Warnings use a region named 'Validation warnings' with a status line (role status). Other error messages keep role alert (D75).
basis: A region can contain an alert; both parts of D75 then hold. Came from the one failing scenario of run 8.
later_change: singular forms and warnings line (D109)

decision: Every integer in a path, query or JSON body is a 32-bit signed integer: version numbers, page and pageSize from 1 to 2147483647 unless a decision sets a lower maximum (pageSize 100, D22). A value outside the range, or one that is not a whole number, gives 400 with the same problem body as other invalid values (D49, D22). The decided contract states format int32 and the maximum.
basis: No project NFR needs more; int32 is the common default of the stack; one rule for path, query and body.
later_change: text form decides (D112)

decision: One backend instance handles at most 4 create or new-version requests at the same time. A fifth gets 503 as D44 with Retry-After 5 and detail 'Too many uploads in progress. Retry later.'. Content validation (D9) and the reference check (D12) run once per request, before the conditional write; a retry of D82 only reads the latest state again and repeats the condition and the update. The heap must hold 4 uploads at the 6 MB request limit (D76) with their parsed form.
basis: Bounds memory at the design load of Q4 (NFR-05); 4 is well above 1 write per second (Q1).

decision: The build validates requests either with a maintained OpenAPI request validator that loads openapi-decided.yaml, or with its own code plus an own test that compares that code with openapi-decided.yaml (every operation, parameter, limit and pattern). The build chooses and says which in REUSE.md. Every own component of more than about 100 lines that does infrastructure work (validation, parsing, caching, query building, HTTP plumbing) has a row in REUSE.md with the product it could have reused and why it did not.
basis: MACH-03 (contract matches behaviour), REUSE-02 and REUSE-07; leaves the build a free but checked choice.
later_change: framework routing (D133)

decision: Unless REUSE.md says why not: SPARQL queries and updates are built with Jena (ParameterizedSparqlString, or the query and update builders), never by joining strings with values; realm keys are fetched and cached with Nimbus JWKSourceBuilder or the Spring Security resource server; W3C trace context and the correlation id run through Micrometer Tracing (D86).
basis: REUSE-01 and REUSE-02; the run 8 design review found all three built by hand.
later_change: own fetch timing around Nimbus for keys (D108)

decision: The finish line includes: mvn verify runs a configured formatter check (Spotless with a fixed style); the UI build runs ESLint and a Prettier check and fails on errors; each UI view has at least one component test (Vitest or similar) in ui/tests that runs in the UI build. A pipeline file is not required (no CI in the factory).
basis: OPS-37 (MUST), CODE-10, CODE-54, CODE-55; cheap gates that a disposable build can still meet.

decision: Logs are JSON lines. Every line carries traceId and correlationId (D86) and operationId from the MDC; a line about a vocabulary also carries vocabularyName and, when known, version, as separate fields. No email or token in logs (D80).
basis: CODE-20, CODE-30; fields make the logs searchable without parsing text.
later_change: stays the log format, Simpl LogWrapper out of scope (D105)

topic: CDM, licence and glossary in the build
decision: The CDM files named in sources.yaml are part of the build input (input/cdm/, from run 9 on). The logical model of D87 uses their class names where the glossary does not decide otherwise and lists each difference. The build ships a LICENSE file with the EUPL 1.2 text and a docs/glossary.md that copies or links the decided glossary.
basis: DATA rules and API-01 need the CDM to be judged; ARCH-08 and DDD-03; the engine now copies the CDM into the run input.
later_change: model differences with the CDM listed (D117)

decision: The local stack may run Keycloak in dev mode, but publishes its port on 127.0.0.1 only. The management port of the backend (D67) is on an internal network of the stack and is not on the front network; step 70 reads metrics through the stack's own scripts. Container CPU and memory limits are variables in the compose file with the current values as defaults.
basis: OWT-A02 and ARCH-14; keeps the stack easy to run on a laptop.
later_change: front network allowed when unpublished and not proxied (D120)

decision: The seed of Q4 is 1000 vocabularies with 20 versions each (20 000 versions), files of about 10 KB. Q1 throughput is an offered rate: the load test sends 20 reads per second and 1 write per second (files up to 1 MB) for 5 minutes; met when the achieved rate is at least 95 % of the offered rate with no errors and the p95 targets hold. The 5 MB writes of D71 run as a separate test, not in the throughput mix.
basis: Makes Q1 and Q4 measurable the same way in every run; run 7 and run 8 used different seeds and mixes.

decision: The vocabulary list has these columns, in this order, with these headers: Name, Status, Description, Creator, Date created, Last updated, Actions. Creator shows createdBy of version 1 (D27); Description the description of the latest version. Sortable columns stay as D23.
basis: SIMPL-18161/AC1 names the creator; D23 and D27 give the rest.

decision: A click on Submit checks every field, touched or not, including an empty Vocabulary file, and shows every error under its field; nothing is sent and the focus moves to the first field with an error (D62). Error texts have reserved space, so an error that appears on blur never moves Submit away from the pointer.
basis: Makes D62 testable and avoids the layout shift run 9 hit.

decision: Q4's sentence on one instance is replaced by D82: the delivered stack must work with two backend instances on one store. The finish line runs the stack with two backends (for example docker compose up --scale backend=2) behind the UI proxy and passes smoke.sh on it. Nothing in the stack fixes a container name or host port per backend.
basis: D82 already makes the service stateless; ARCH-07.

decision: Resilience4j circuit breakers around the store calls and the key fetch. Each opens when at least half of the last 20 calls failed (at least 10 calls), stays open 10 s, then lets 3 probe calls through. While open the caller gets 503 as D44 at once, without waiting for a timeout. Breaker state is in the metrics (D86).
basis: CODE-46, ARCH-34; Resilience4j is the usual Spring choice.
later_change: store 5xx counts (D134)

decision: No shared Simpl exception library is used. The problem types of D48 are the error codes: the build has one exception base class carrying the problem type, title and status, and one handler that maps it to problem+json.
basis: CODE-33 and CODE-44 are met by one base class; the library is not available to the factory.

decision: The Simpl log format (LogWrapper) and log shipping are out of scope for the factory's builds, because the library is not in the build input. The JSON lines of D96 are the format. The build records CODE-21, CODE-52 and SEC-11 as deviations with this decision as reason.
basis: Not available to the factory; D96 gives the fields a shipper needs.

decision: The uploaded file stays in the RDF store, next to its metadata, so one store transaction holds both (D8). The build may store it as one literal or in chunks. Object storage is not used: at 5 MB per file and the Q4 load it adds a second store without need.
basis: E3 (same persistence as Schema Management), D8 all or nothing, REUSE-05 recorded.

topic: No host port for the store
decision: D83 wins: the store publishes no host port, also not for debugging. The build profile drops the Fuseki port; debugging goes through docker exec or the backup scripts.

topic: Realm keys: library and first fetch
decision: D94 is changed for keys: the build uses Nimbus JWKSet and JWSVerifier with its own fetch timing, so D88's cooldown and outcomes hold. The first fetch may be lazy, on the first token; until then GET /health reports UP when the store answers, and DEGRADED only after a fetch failed.
basis: D88 is the behaviour that counts; the library serves it.
later_change: claims via library (D132)

decision: Errors line: '1 error found' or '<n> errors found', role alert. Warnings line: '1 warning found' or '<n> warnings found', role status, as the first line of the region 'Validation warnings'.
basis: Plain English; completes D90.

decision: Decided as run 9 built them: a JSON body over 1 MB gives 413; more than 64 multipart parts give 400; a date-time without an offset is read as UTC; the 201 body carries createdBy and latestVersionHref; aliasUris is always present in responses (empty list allowed); a bad element of a search array is named '<array>[<index>]' in the issue; paging links put page and pageSize first, then the other parameters in request order. These are added to the D79 list.
basis: The build's choices are sound and now shared by both writers.

decision: Every paging link (self, first, prev, next, last) carries page and pageSize, also when the request did not send them, with the values used.
basis: Links are then exact and comparable; D78.

decision: The text decides: an integer in a path or query is one or more digits, nothing else ('2.0', '1e1', '+2' and ' 2' give 400). In a JSON body it is a JSON number without fraction or exponent.
basis: Simplest rule to build and test; D91.

decision: After a successful new version from the Update form, the UI opens the details page of that vocabulary with the new version's panel open, and shows the D14 notification and warnings there, as D72 does after a create.
basis: Same flow as create.

decision: A load error or a failed status change shows one element with role alert that holds the decided text followed by the problem detail.
basis: One announcement per event; simple to test.

decision: The list has buttons 'Previous page' and 'Next page' and the text 'Page <n> of <m>'. The deprecation banner on the details page has role status and the D36 text.
basis: Accessible names that both writers can use (D75).

decision: Added to the D79 list and to openapi-decided.yaml: format date or date-time on the date filters (D20), the Turtle media type text/turtle on vocabularyFile (D9), and minimum 1 on the version in paths (D49).
basis: So fuzzing tells decided rejections from defects.

decision: The CDM findings go to the CDM owner; the build does not wait for them. The logical model of D87 and D97 uses typed attributes, leaves search request classes out of the domain model, names timestamps creationDate and lastUpdateDate (glossary), and lists each difference with the CDM.
basis: The factory judges the spec; the build follows the glossary.

decision: The whole text 'Latest ACTIVE version: <n>' is one link to that version.
basis: The suite reads it that way; one link is the clearer target.

topic: Parallel writes in the D43 test
decision: D92 stays: a fifth upload on one instance gets 503. The D43 test sends at most 4 parallel new versions.
basis: Keeps the memory bound; the test still shows serialised writes.

decision: The management port may sit on the front network when it is published on no host port and the proxy never forwards /actuator. Step 70 reads metrics from inside the stack.
basis: Docker limits; the intent of D98 (not reachable from outside) still holds.

decision: The 400 for a part with an empty name is dropped from D70. The container ignores such a part; the request is judged without it. No own multipart parser.
basis: REUSE-02 outweighs this edge case.

decision: The proxy's body limit is 7 MB, above D76, so the service decides on sizes. Where the proxy answers itself (TRACE, malformed request, above 7 MB) it returns problem+json with the D48 type and status (405, 400, 413).
basis: One error format for the whole component (D48).

decision: The UI sends Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' and the identity provider URL; no inline scripts or styles; frame-ancestors 'none'. UI tests run axe with the browser's CSP bypass.
basis: OWASP headers; tests should not weaken the product.

decision: For an external vocabulary file the namespace URI is the base for relative IRIs.
basis: Same rule as D57.

decision: The validation report holds at most 1000 issues. When there are more, it holds the first 1000 in file order and the problem body has "truncated": true. Added to D79.
basis: Bounds response size (NFR-04).

decision: HEAD and OPTIONS on declared paths get 405 with an Allow header, like other undeclared methods (D67). The UI is same-origin through the proxy, so no CORS.
basis: Confirms the build; one rule for undeclared methods.

decision: application/* is accepted like */*; the response uses the operation's normal media type.
basis: HTTP media ranges; nothing to gain from refusing it.

decision: Status sorts alphabetically: ACTIVE before DEPRECATED ascending. This is also the business order.
basis: Both orders agree; no extra rule needed.

topic: Unknown key after a failed fetch
decision: Inside the 10 s window after a failed key fetch, an unknown key id gives 503 (keys not available, D44). After a successful fetch it gives 401 (D88).
basis: The caller can tell 'retry later' from 'bad token'.

decision: An offset beyond plus or minus 18:00 gives 400, like any invalid date (D20).
basis: ISO 8601 and java.time limits.

decision: The build profile names bash stack.sh up as the start command; stack.sh creates the local secrets. The .env file is never committed.
basis: Secrets stay out of the profile (OPS-11).

decision: Issuer, audience, expiry and not-before are checked with Nimbus DefaultJWTClaimsVerifier or Spring Security JwtValidators. Own code only for the key fetch timing of D88.
basis: REUSE-01; D108 kept own code for timing only.

decision: Requests are routed with Spring MVC mappings that declare produces and consumes; query parameters are bound by the framework, with the strict checks of D52 on top. An own test fixes the order 404, 405, 406, 415.
basis: REUSE-06 and REUSE-07; run 10 built a second request layer.

decision: A store 5xx and a timeout count as breaker failures; a 4xx from the store does not. GET /v1/health never fetches keys; it reports the cached key state and checks the store with one bounded call.
basis: MSV-06; health must not be a way around D88.

decision: No interface for a class with one implementation; CODE-11 is a recorded deviation with this decision as reason.
basis: The code is disposable; ports-and-adapters rules are excluded on purpose.

decision: The read p95 of Q1 holds per operation, including the paged list at the full D99 seed.
basis: A slow list hurts users even when the mix looks fine.

topic: Issue name for an empty array
decision: The issue is named after the array (namespaceUris or aliasUris), in body.
basis: Points the client at the field.

decision: Exactly one issue, in query, named after the parameter.
basis: Simple and testable.

topic: Known method on a declared path
decision: A known method that the path does not declare (for example PUT /vocabularies) gets 405 with Allow, with or without a token. 405 comes before 401 (D67).
basis: D67 already orders 405 before 401.
